title: Supervisor never reaps spawned workers — zombies accumulate under needle supervise (GH #12)
description:
Reported 2026-07-28 by jarvis-laboratories (same production adopter as GH #7-#11 / ADR-009), same ~900-bead monorepo cutover. GitHub issue: https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/12. Full rationale: ADR-010 (docs/adr/010-supervisor-zombie-reaping.md), plan.md Phase 14.1.

Confirmed against source: Supervisor::spawn_worker (src/supervisor/mod.rs:377-498) builds a detached child (setsid via pre_exec, process_group(0), null stdio) and calls cmd.spawn()? (line 488) with the returned std::process::Child immediately dropped — never bound to a variable, so there is no way to later .wait()/.try_wait() on it. setsid/process_group detach the child from the controlling terminal/session only; they do NOT detach it from being a reapable child of the supervisor process. A crate-wide grep for waitpid|try_wait|SIGCHLD|\.wait() finds reaping logic only in src/dispatch/mod.rs, src/telemetry/mod.rs, src/canary/mod.rs — all different child processes (agent dispatch, telemetry subprocess, canary binary checks), none of them supervisor-spawned workers. Rust's Child::drop does not reap a process.

Production evidence (reporter's cutover soak, pin v0.2.12/fad0b50): 22 [needle ...] <defunct> zombies under needle-supervise after ~15 minutes of operation.

Suggested fix (already validated as a local patch in the reporter's production fork, and the decision in ADR-010): add a reap sweep at the top of Supervisor::tick() (src/supervisor/mod.rs) — loop libc::waitpid(-1, &mut status, libc::WNOHANG) until it returns 0 (nothing left to reap right now) or -1 with errno == ECHILD (no children at all). Safe because needle supervise only ever directly spawns worker processes; gate commands/dispatch subprocesses run inside the worker process (a separate PID tree), so this cannot race with the .wait() calls already present elsewhere for different child processes.

Alternatives considered and rejected in ADR-010: double-fork + reparent to init (bigger change than needed); retaining Child handles + try_wait per tick (would require new Supervisor state for no benefit over the sweep, since nothing else needs live child handles).

Acceptance criteria:
- Supervisor::tick() reaps any exited worker child within one poll_interval_secs tick — no zombie process-table entries accumulate for the lifetime of a long-running needle supervise daemon.
- Regression test: spawn a real short-lived child (e.g. true), let it exit, assert it is a zombie before the sweep runs, assert the sweep reaps it.
- No change to spawn_worker's detach model (setsid + process_group(0)) — this is a missing-reap fix, not a re-architecture.
- cargo test --lib passes; no clippy warnings; needle-ci green on push.
close_reason: Fixed by 81b0995 (bf-z3yp0): Supervisor::tick() now sweeps waitpid(-1, WNOHANG) at the top of every tick, reaping exited worker children so they no longer accumulate as <defunct> zombies. GH #12.

description: Add a safe timeout-to-mitosis lifecycle for beads whose agent work reaches a legacy wall-clock or hard execution deadline while making progress. title: Worker prompt template emits 'br close', silently leaking every bead on hosts without the br shim
description:
Found 2026-08-02 provisioning bench (NixOS) as a second needle host.

The dispatch prompt needle writes to /tmp/needle/prompt-<bead>-<pid>.md ends with:

    Close the bead:
    `br close <bead-id>`

'br' is the deprecated alias; the canonical CLI is 'bf'. On this server br
survives only as a shim at ~/.local/bin/br that logs the caller and execs bf,
so the instruction happens to work and the bug is invisible.

On a fresh host there is no shim. The agent runs 'br close', gets
command-not-found, and the bead stays in_progress forever. Observed on bench
before the shim was copied over: worker bench-screenferry-1 claimed 4 beads in
~15 minutes and closed zero. Telemetry showed 4 bead.claim.succeeded and no
bead.closed / bead.released events at all; the state machine ran
SELECTING -> BUILDING -> DISPATCHING -> EXECUTING -> HANDLING -> LOGGING and
looped straight back to SELECTING.

This is very likely a contributor to the 372 beads sitting in_progress across
49 workspaces on this server, many assigned to workers that no longer exist.

Evidence that needle is the last br consumer: ~/.local/state/br-deprecation.log
has 19,560 entries, 19,543 of them caller=needle-* and only 17 caller=bash.
Fixing this unblocks retiring the alias entirely.

Fix: emit 'bf close' in the prompt template. Grep the template source for
'br close' and any other 'br ' subcommand invocations.

Acceptance: a worker on a host with no br on PATH closes a bead successfully.
close_reason: Fixed and released in v0.2.16 (commit 84b17f5). Pluck template now emits 'bf close'; split template uses 'bf create --title/--description/--label'; BrCliBeadStore::discover() resolves bf before falling back to br. Verified in the shipped binary: 'bf close {bead_id}' present, zero occurrences of 'br close'. needle-ci green at 1704 passed / 0 failed (workflow needle-ci-debug-gtl2n).

title: 16.3 CliBeadStore — one descriptor-driven BeadStore impl; delete the two existing stores
description:
One BeadStore impl driven by a BeadBackend descriptor: renders argv from templates, dispatches on strategy, parses per the declared shape.

BrCliBeadStore and BfCliBeadStore are DELETED, not refactored. Their behavior survives as builtin descriptors. This is what makes the ADR-013 section 5 chimera unconstructible: argv and binary come from one descriptor, so no store can hold beads_rust argv and a bf binary simultaneously.

title: routing: strict mode — fail loudly when no rule matches an unrecognized model
description:
## Problem

When agent.routing.rules is configured but no rule matches the active model, NEEDLE silently falls back to agent.default (or routing.default_adapter if set). This means a misconfigured or unrecognized model (e.g. a new provider, a typo, a model removed from the adapter list) routes silently to the wrong adapter with no signal to the operator.

## What to add

Add an optional boolean agent.routing.strict (default: false):

  agent:
    routing:
      strict: true
      rules:
        - match_model: "(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*"
          adapter: claude-print
        - match_model: "glm.*"
          adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7

When strict: true and no rule matches the active model:
1. Do NOT fall back to agent.default or routing.default_adapter.
2. Emit a RoutingFailed telemetry event with the model name and rule count.
3. Return Err from apply_routing_rules with a clear human-readable message:
   "no routing rule matched model 'gpt-4o' — add a rule to agent.routing.rules or set routing.strict: false to fall back to the default adapter"
4. Propagates through resolve_adapter -> dispatch -> marks the bead as failed (not orphaned), surfaced in the bead list.

## Schema changes

pub struct RoutingConfig {
    pub rules: Vec<RoutingRule>,
    pub default_adapter: Option<String>,
    pub strict: bool,  // new, default false
}

Add RoutingFailed to EventKind:
RoutingFailed {
    bead_id: BeadId,
    model: String,
    rules_tried: usize,
}

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] RoutingConfig has strict: bool (default false); existing configs without strict behave unchanged.
- [ ] strict: true + no match: apply_routing_rules returns Err with the message above; RoutingFailed telemetry emitted.
- [ ] strict: false + no match: existing fallback behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Bead is marked failed (dispatch error), not orphaned or silently retried.
- [ ] Unit tests: strict=true no-match -> Err; strict=false no-match -> default; strict=true match -> Ok.
- [ ] cargo test passes (push and wait for needle-ci).

while RAM barely moves -- CPU churn from repeated scanning of workspaces with no claimable work,

scanned N times in a row with zero claimable candidates found" -- it re-scans on the same cadence
regardless of hit rate. Add an adaptive backoff: track consecutive empty-scan cycles per worker
(in-memory is fine, does not need to survive restart) and geometrically increase the delay before
the next Explore pass (e.g. base interval up to some capped ceiling, e.g. 8x), resetting to base
the moment any candidate is found. Must not change the "no claimable beads" outcome-visibility for
strand escalation (Mend/Weave/etc. still evaluated in order) -- only the re-scan cadence within
Explore itself.

Acceptance criteria: a fixture simulating N consecutive empty Explore scans shows the effective
scan interval increasing up to the configured ceiling and resetting to base on the next
scan that finds a candidate; a regression test pins CPU-relevant behavior (call frequency, not
wall-clock) so it's testable without real sleeps.

Child beads cover: dependency lockfile, prebuilt builder image, sccache, split
verify/release stages, retry-strategy fix, and the test-suite changes that are

Two workflow-template children live in the declarative-config repo, not here:
k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml. Those go through ArgoCD
(edit manifest, commit, push, let it sync) -- never kubectl apply.

title: 16.11 Document per-backend capability gaps where operators will see them
description:
The three backends are not feature-equivalent, and two of the gaps change fleet SAFETY rather than just convenience. These must be visible in operator-facing docs, not buried in code comments.

Gaps to document (docs/configuration.md and README backend section):
- Atomic mitosis is bf-ONLY. br and bead have no transactional batch, so split_bead falls back to the non-atomic default with its orphaned-child crash window (a crash between create and dep add leaves a child orphaned and the parent permanently blocked).
- Atomic server-side claim is bf- and bead-only. beads_rust has NO claim subcommand, so claim_auto is a read-then-write with a real TOCTOU window between ready and update. Two workers on the same beads_rust workspace can claim the same bead. This is the duplicate-claim failure mode CLAUDE.md already calls out as the real hazard in fleet dispatch.
- Velocity-aware claim scoring (--model/--harness/--harness-version) is bf-only; worker_sessions/velocity_stats rows are not written on other backends.

Deliverables:
- A capability matrix in docs/configuration.md matching ADR-013 section 2.
- `needle doctor` surfaces the active backend gaps, so an operator sees them without reading docs.

Acceptance criteria:
- An operator choosing a backend can see, before deploying a fleet, that beads_rust has no atomic claim.

See ADR-013 section 2 and Consequences.

title: 16.2 Implement the operation-strategy set (six enums, once each)
description:
The part a flat argv table cannot express, and the reason ADR-013 drafts 1-2 reached for hardcoded impls. Implement each strategy ONCE; descriptors select among them.

- claim:      compare_and_set | batch_op
- claim_auto: atomic_subcommand | non_atomic_scan
- split:      transactional_batch | sequential
- create->ID: bare_id | json_field
- labels:     csv | repeated
- import:     bare | input_plus_mode

Mapping across the three shipped backends:
  br   claim=compare_and_set  claim_auto=non_atomic_scan   split=sequential            labels=csv       import=bare
  bf   claim=batch_op         claim_auto=atomic_subcommand split=transactional_batch   labels=repeated  import=bare
  bead claim=compare_and_set  claim_auto=atomic_subcommand split=sequential            labels=repeated  import=input_plus_mode

These six cover every divergence observed across three independently-evolving upstreams plus their Go ancestor (bd 0.49.6). A backend needing genuinely new behavior adds ONE variant — available to every backend — not a BeadStore impl.

Deliverables:
- Each strategy implemented once, with the race semantics documented per variant. non_atomic_scan in particular has a REAL TOCTOU window (ready -> update); it is not merely a slower atomic_subcommand.
- Unknown strategy name in a descriptor is a load-time validation error naming the file and the operation.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test per strategy variant, independent of any particular backend.
- compare_and_set proven to detect a lost race (bead claimed by another actor between read and write).
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

See ADR-013 Decision section 2.

title: Unbounded per-bead events list causes runaway git bloat (no compaction tool)

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Found 2026-08-11 during a lab incident investigation: bead bf-5vfu in the domain-check repo ("Investigate br claim exclusion logic") accumulated 973,589 events in its events list — almost entirely repeating claimed/assignee_changed pairs from a claim-race/retry loop. This inflated that single bead's JSON record to 246MB (out of a 352-bead, 247MB total .beads/issues.jsonl). The bloated file was committed 153 times, growing domain-check's .git to 4.1GB, and is a strong suspect in a series of git-process OOM kills on lab (7x, 07:32-07:55 EDT, each ~12-13GB RSS) that ultimately took the whole NEEDLE tmux fleet down.

Root gap: NEEDLE/bf never caps or prunes the per-bead events list, so any bead caught in a claim-race loop becomes a ticking git-bloat time bomb once its bead store gets committed. Checked 'bf --help' end to end — no compact/vacuum/prune-events command exists to fix this after the fact either. The 'compaction_level' field on the bead schema suggests this was anticipated but never implemented/wired up.

Could not fix bf-5vfu itself: trimming it would mean hand-editing .beads/issues.jsonl directly, which is a hard prohibition in this environment (must go through bf, never edit .beads/ by hand), and there is no bf command that does it instead.

Suggested fixes: (1) cap events-per-bead in bf/br (e.g. hard limit + oldest-N-dropped or summarized), (2) surface a bf command to compact/truncate a bead's event history, (3) NEEDLE-side: detect and circuit-break a claim-race loop before it can generate hundreds of thousands of events on one bead.

title: bf_cli_bead_store_list_all_passes_explicit_limit is flaky under parallel load
description:
Found 2026-08-02 during the v0.2.16 release.

bead_store::tests::bf_cli_bead_store_list_all_passes_explicit_limit fails
intermittently in a full 'cargo test --lib' run:

  panicked at src/bead_store/mod.rs:2707:
  called Result::unwrap() on an Err value:
  Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound } -- reading back bf-list-args.txt

The test writes a fake 'bf' shell script into a tempdir, chmods it 0755, calls
list_all(), then reads the args file the script should have written. When it
fails, that file does not exist, i.e. the fake script never ran or never
completed its write.

Passes 3/3 in isolation and passed a second full-suite run (1704/0), so it is
load-dependent, not deterministic. Observed failing in one full local run and
suspected as the third failure in CI workflow needle-ci-manual-x9r67 (which
reported 3 failures where an isolated local run reproduced only 2).

Fix direction: the test already notes it uses a test-specific args file 'to
avoid race conditions', so the remaining race is likely exec-vs-write of the
script itself under load. Consider fsync/close-before-exec, or asserting on
list_all()'s Result instead of ignoring it with 'let _' so the real error
surfaces instead of a downstream NotFound.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: Root-caused 2026-08-06: this is a wall-clock timing bug, not a logic bug. Evidence: passes 1711/1711 in a full local --lib run on ex44 (692.81s at a 2-core cap) and passes in 0.00s in isolation; fails only on iad-ci, which takes 1311-1542s for the same suite at a 3-core limit -- about 2x the wall clock for 50 percent more CPU. It failed both runs on 2026-08-06 (needle-ci-x2wx2, needle-ci-vnmhd), blocking every release. The test also hides its own cause: "let _ = store.list_all().await;" discards the real error, so the failure surfaces as an unrelated NotFound panic on the args file -- changing that to .expect() is the fastest way to learn which shared-state interaction loses the race. Raised P3 to P1 because it blocks all releases. Real fix tracked as bf-4icmm (virtual time), which now blocks this bead; see also bf-hu2ag (per-test HOME isolation), since the suite writes into the live fleet state dir.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: MEASURED FLAKE RATE 2026-08-06: 4 failures in 7 CI runs (57%). All four are this identical test, and all four panic at the same line -- src/bead_store/mod.rs:2736:56, which is "let args = std::fs::read_to_string(&args_file).unwrap();". Failed: needle-ci-x2wx2, needle-ci-vnmhd, needle-ci-f46kr, needle-ci-verify-xjbbm. Passed: needle-ci-8x2jj, needle-ci-kz4qz, needle-ci-xt8tz. Test-suite runtime on the runs that completed: 1243s-1540s. This confirms the earlier diagnosis exactly: the panic is on the args-file read, not on any assertion, because "let _ = store.list_all().await;" one line earlier discarded the real error. It also confirms it is nondeterministic rather than a hard break -- the same commit both passes and fails. At a 57% failure rate this is not an occasional annoyance; it is the dominant reason NEEDLE releases do not ship. Fix is bf-4icmm (virtual time), which blocks this bead.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-07 — and it is NOT the wall-clock timing theory recorded above. That theory was wrong. The real error is ETXTBSY (Text file busy, os error 26) on subprocess spawn: the test writes a fake bf script, chmods it, and execs it while a concurrent fork holds an inherited write fd. Reproduced 15 times in 40 runs (37.5 percent) with "cargo test --lib bead_store::tests -- --test-threads=32". Full analysis in bf-37hoj; fix in bf-2um4a, which now blocks this bead instead of bf-4icmm. Virtual time would not have fixed this.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
RETARGETED 2026-08-11 — descriptor design supersedes the module split.

Original scope was "split mod.rs into br_cli.rs / bf_cli.rs / bead_cli.rs". Under ADR-013 draft 3 there are no per-backend impls to split into: BrCliBeadStore and BfCliBeadStore are DELETED and replaced by one descriptor-driven CliBeadStore.

NEW SCOPE — the BeadBackend descriptor type and its loader, modeled directly on the agent-adapter precedent at src/dispatch/mod.rs:570-660:
- Serde struct: name, binary, detect_paths, identity_pattern, version_command, per-operation specs, declared capabilities.
- builtin_bead_backends() returning the three shipped descriptors as data.
- load_bead_backends() merging ~/.config/needle/bead-backends/*.yaml, user files overriding built-ins BY NAME — same contract as load_adapters.
- Config knob: bead_cli.backend (auto | descriptor name) + optional explicit path, overridable per workspace in .needle.yaml.

CRITICAL: validate at LOAD time, not first claim. Reject unknown strategies, unresolvable {placeholders}, missing required operations. A malformed descriptor is now the way a fleet breaks — it must fail at startup, loudly, naming the file.

mod.rs still keeps the trait, shared types, parse helpers, ETXTBSY spawn retry, and corruption detection. That part of the original scope survives.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
ADD 2026-08-11 — descriptors must carry `verified_against`.

The br binary installed on ex44 is v0.1.28 (built 2026-03-29). Upstream beads_rust is v0.2.22 (2026-08-06) — ~20 releases and 4 months ahead. A fleet host running a stale binary while upstream moves is normal and expected.

So the BeadBackend struct needs:
- verified_against: the binary version string the descriptor was authored against
- verified_on: date
- for backends with no release artifacts (bead-rs is Forgejo-only, no GitHub releases): a commit SHA instead of a version

`needle bead-backend <name>` (bf-1hc0r) compares verified_against to the resolved binary version and WARNS on mismatch. It must not hard-fail — a stale-but-compatible binary is the common case — but silence is not acceptable either.

Also correcting the capability surface: br 0.2.22 gained `capabilities` and `robot-docs` (0.1.28 had only `schema`). All three backends now expose a capabilities-style contract, so negotiation is uniform rather than a bead-rs special case.

title: Retry ETXTBSY on every bead_store spawn path, and stop discarding spawn errors in tests
description:
Fix for bf-37hoj (ETXTBSY on subprocess spawn). Two parts; part 1 alone
resolves the CI flake, part 2 prevents the next one from being misdiagnosed.

PART 1 — treat ETXTBSY as transient on every spawn path (the actual fix)

spawn_version_check (~line 68 of src/bead_store/mod.rs) already does this
correctly and its doc comment already describes the race. Generalise that
handling; do not invent a new pattern.

  Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < MAX_ATTEMPTS => {
      tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
  }

Apply at all four unprotected spawn sites:
  - run_br_in    (~line 567, spawn at ~579)
  - run_bf_batch (~line 850, spawn at ~864)
  - run_bf_claim (~line 887, spawn at ~926)
  - run_bf_in    (~line 1591, spawn at ~1608)

run_bf_in and run_br_in already own a retry loop for transient lock errors, but
the spawn is outside it — cmd.spawn()...? returns immediately. Route the spawn
error into that existing loop rather than bolting on a second one: ETXTBSY is
transient in exactly the same sense a lock error is. Keep the existing behaviour
that genuinely non-transient spawn errors (ENOENT, EACCES) still fail fast and
are NOT retried — retrying a missing binary five times only slows the failure.

This is a production fix, not just a test fix. NEEDLE hot-reloads its own binary
and upgrades bf in place, so a worker spawning bf or needle mid-rewrite hits the
same errno and currently fails the whole operation.

PART 2 — stop discarding the error that explains the failure

Four tests do "let _ = store.<call>().await;" one line before asserting on a
file that call was supposed to produce (~lines 2458, 2506, 2559, 2733). Because
workspace and args_file are the same tempdir, the discarded error and the panic
have the same underlying cause, but only the misleading one is reported. Replace
each with .expect("..."), so any future spawn failure names itself instead of
surfacing as an unrelated NotFound.

The two exclude_ids tests (panics at ~2604 and ~2667) follow the same shape and
should get the same treatment.

ACCEPTANCE
  - cargo test --lib bead_store::tests -- --test-threads=32, run 40 times,
    produces 0 failures. Baseline before the fix was 15/40 (37.5 percent).
  - No test in this file discards a Result whose failure it then asserts on.
  - A deliberately missing binary still fails immediately, not after 5 retries.

DO NOT bother converting these tests to tokio virtual time (bf-4icmm). That was
based on the earlier wall-clock theory, which bf-37hoj disproves — the failure
is an exec race, not a timeout, and virtual time would not have fixed it.

title: cargo test --lib hangs indefinitely on strand::explore deadlock_scenario_* tests
description:
Discovered 2026-07-28 while validating the GH #7-#11 fix (commit e97e88a / 4d8820f). `cargo test --lib` hangs indefinitely (near-zero CPU, zero log progress for 5+ minutes) on 4 tests in src/strand/explore.rs:
- strand::explore::tests::deadlock_scenario_assigned_beads_allow_advancement
- strand::explore::tests::deadlock_scenario_excluded_and_assigned_beads_allow_advancement
- strand::explore::tests::deadlock_scenario_excluded_beads_allow_advancement
- strand::explore::tests::nonexistent_workspace_path_returns_no_work

Reproduced independently in two separate environments:
1. Local (this server): cargo test --lib ran 50+ minutes with zero output progress before being killed (cgroup-limited run, CPUQuota=200%).
2. iad-ci workflow needle-ci-g7cqh (triggered by push of commit e97e88a to main): pod CPU usage measured at 1m (essentially idle) for 5+ minutes with these 4 tests stuck at 'has been running for over 60 seconds' and no further log lines appearing after. This is NOT slow-but-progressing (that would show real CPU usage from repeated lock-retry attempts) -- it looks like a genuine deadlock (a task waiting on something that never resolves), or a thread-pool-starvation cascade where these 4 stuck test threads exhaust the test harness's thread pool and block all other pending tests from ever running.

Root cause NOT yet investigated. src/strand/explore.rs has not been touched by any of the last 5+ commits (confirmed via git log), so this is pre-existing and unrelated to the GH #7-#11 fix or to any of the prerequisite compile-breakage fixes bundled in commit e97e88a (missing tsnet module wiring, MitosisConfig.max_depth, AgentAdapter test fixtures). Given CLAUDE.md documents that CI (needle-ci WorkflowTemplate) runs 'cargo test --lib' as its gating step, this hang means needle-ci will never reach the Succeeded phase for ANY future push until fixed -- it is not specific to this branch/commit.

The tests use a mock store factory (search 'DeadlockMockStoreFactory' in src/strand/explore.rs) and call strand.evaluate(&store).await inside a #[tokio::test] (default current-thread runtime). Worth checking: (a) whether ExploreStrand::evaluate or the mock factory has a genuine lock/channel deadlock under current-thread scheduling, (b) whether these tests ever passed in CI historically -- main did not even compile before this session's prerequisite fixes, so it is possible nobody has run the full suite to completion in some time and this has been silently broken for a while, (c) whether RUST_TEST_THREADS or --test-threads settings change the symptom.

Acceptance criteria: cargo test --lib completes (reaches 'test result: ... finished in Ns') without hanging, on both local and iad-ci; the 4 named tests either pass or are fixed/quarantined with a documented reason; needle-ci reaches Succeeded on a subsequent push.

title: Worker startup: validate configured adapter exists before accepting work
description:
Even after bf-14w removes the silent fallback in resolve_adapter, a worker with a misconfigured adapter will fail only at dispatch time (after claiming a bead). It should fail at startup, before claiming any beads.

## What to add

In the worker initialization path (before the main loop begins), call resolve_adapter() once as a preflight check:

  // In Worker::new() or the run() entry point, before the claim loop:
  self.resolve_adapter().context("startup adapter preflight failed")?;

If this returns Err, the worker should exit immediately with a clear error message printed to stderr:
  'NEEDLE: agent adapter "claude-code-glm-47" not found — aborting. Check ~/.needle/agents/ or the agents config directory.'

This prevents a worker from running for hours, repeatedly claiming and failing beads, when the adapter was never configured correctly.

## Complete when
- Starting needle with --agent nonexistent-adapter exits immediately with a clear error (not after the first bead claim)
- The error message names the missing adapter and suggests where to look
- cargo test passes (push to main and wait for needle-ci)

title: Set non-zero default budget.warn_usd/stop_usd or warn loudly when both are unset
description:
src/cost/mod.rs implements budget enforcement (warn at warn_usd, halt workers at stop_usd) but
both gate on "> 0.0" -- the shipped default (and this repo's own live .needle.yaml) is
warn_usd: 0.0, stop_usd: 0.0, which is silently interpreted as "no cap, no warning, ever." A
fleet operator who hasn't separately set up claude-governor (README: "resource governance is
delegated to claude-governor" -- a different, opt-in tool) gets fully unbounded spend with zero
guardrail and zero indication anything is unconfigured.

Deliverable (pick one, whichever is less surprising to an existing operator -- discuss/decide in
the bead, don't silently pick):
(a) Ship a conservative non-zero default for stop_usd/warn_usd in Config::default()
    (src/config/mod.rs) so a fresh install has a real guardrail out of the box, or
(b) Keep 0.0 meaning "unset" but have worker startup (or `needle doctor`) print a one-time loud
    warning when both are 0.0, so an operator knows spend is fully uncapped rather than assuming
    NEEDLE is protecting them.

Acceptance criteria: a fresh .needle.yaml (via `needle init`) either ships a real budget cap, or
a worker/doctor run makes it unmistakable that none is configured. Existing configs that
deliberately set 0.0 are not silently overridden without the operator's action.

title: Model-based adapter routing: Anthropic subscription models -> claude-print, default claude-code-glm-4.7 (June 15 deadline)
description:
## Context (recreated 2026-06-11 — original bead chain bf-22v/bf-6hp/bf-2pp was lost in a workspace rebuild)

DEADLINE: June 15, 2026 — Anthropic Agent SDK credit split. After that date, plain `claude -p` dispatches bill API credits instead of subscription.

Policy (user-set): claude-print is the default adapter ONLY for Anthropic claude models on subscription billing — sonnet, opus, fable, haiku. ALL other models default to the existing `claude-code-glm-4.7` adapter.

## Current state
Adapter selection is adapter-name-static per worker (Worker::resolve_adapter, src/worker/mod.rs ~line 2812): config.agent.default -> workspace .needle.yaml -> env -> CLI. The model is a field ON the adapter; model never influences adapter choice. The claude-print adapter yaml is already installed at ~/.config/needle/adapters/claude-print.yaml and the binary works (~/.local/bin/claude-print).

## Implement
1. Config schema: `agent.routing` — ordered list of {model_pattern (regex/glob), adapter} rules, first-match-wins, workspace-overridable via .needle.yaml; `default_adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7` fallback.
2. Ship default rules: pattern matching anthropic claude sonnet/opus/fable/haiku model names -> claude-print.
3. Apply routing in resolve_adapter/dispatch when a model is requested; emit a routing-decision telemetry event (model, matched rule, chosen adapter).
4. NO silent fallback: if the routed adapter is missing, fail the dispatch loudly (complements bf-14w and bf-2wi — do not duplicate their scope).
5. Update docs/plan.md with the routing policy + June 15 rationale.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit tests: pattern matching, first-match-wins, workspace override, default fallback.
- [ ] Requesting a sonnet/opus/fable/haiku model routes to claude-print; glm-4.7 routes to claude-code-glm-4.7.
- [ ] Missing routed adapter = loud dispatch failure (no builtin claude-sonnet fallback).

title: ETXTBSY on subprocess spawn: run_br_in/run_bf_in never retry 'Text file busy', flaking 6 bead_store tests
description:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND REPRODUCED 2026-08-07. Supersedes the "wall-clock timing"
theory recorded on bf-2mp0y — that was wrong.

The real error, captured by temporarily replacing the discarded Result with a
print:

  failed to spawn bf subprocess: ["list", "--json", "--limit", "999999"]
  Caused by:
      Text file busy (os error 26)
      root = Os { code: 26, kind: ExecutableFileBusy, message: "Text file busy" }

REPRODUCTION (deterministic enough to iterate on):

  cargo test --lib bead_store::tests -- --test-threads=32

run in a loop 40x produced 15 failing runs — a 37.5 percent per-run failure
rate. It does NOT reproduce at default thread counts, which is why the suite
looks green locally and red on the smaller CI node.

MECHANISM. These tests write a fake bf/br shell script, chmod 0755 it, then
execute it. Linux fails execve with ETXTBSY if ANY process holds the file open
for writing. Rust opens files O_CLOEXEC, but fork/posix_spawn still leaves a
window: a concurrently spawning test forks, the child inherits the writing
testfixture fd, and until that child reaches execve the script counts as "open
for writing". Any test exec-ing its own freshly written script in that window
gets ETXTBSY. 11 sites in this file write+chmod+exec a script, so the window is
hit often once tests run concurrently.

WHY THE SYMPTOM LOOKED UNRELATED. In each of these tests the workspace and the
args file are the SAME directory (workspace = tmp_dir.path(), args_file =
tmp_dir.path().join(..)), and the spawn error is discarded by
"let _ = store.list_all().await;". The fake script therefore never runs, never
writes the args file, and the next line panics on
read_to_string(&args_file).unwrap() with a bare
Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound }. The genuine ETXTBSY is thrown away one line
earlier. Every CI failure has been reported by this misleading NotFound.

AFFECTED TESTS (observed failing across 40 runs):
  7x bf_cli_bead_store_list_all_passes_explicit_limit
  4x br_cli_bead_store_ready_passes_explicit_limit
  2x br_cli_bead_store_ready_filters_by_exclude_ids
  2x bf_cli_bead_store_ready_passes_explicit_limit
  2x bf_cli_bead_store_ready_filters_by_exclude_ids
  1x br_cli_bead_store_list_all_passes_large_explicit_limit

NOT ONLY A TEST BUG. run_bf_in (~line 1591) and run_br_in (~line 567) both do
cmd.spawn()? with no ETXTBSY handling, and so do run_bf_batch (~864) and
run_bf_claim (~926). NEEDLE hot-reloads its own binaries and upgrades bf in
place, so a worker that spawns bf or needle while that file is being rewritten
hits exactly this errno in production and fails the operation outright.

The fix already exists in this same file and was simply never generalised:
spawn_version_check (~line 68) retries raw_os_error()==Some(26) five times with
a 20ms backoff, and its doc comment describes this precise race. Only the
--version path is protected.

Solution tracked separately.

title: Mitosis: add repeat_interval to trigger re-split on consecutive failures
description:
## Problem

`MitosisConfig.first_failure_only` (default: true) means mitosis only fires on failure #1.
Beads that fail repeatedly after the first attempt loop forever with thousands of failures
and no re-split. Seen in practice: bf-27p7 at 1650+ failures, mta-my-way-rq9 at 2050+.

`force_failure_threshold` exists but fires on every failure >= N — too noisy.

## Work

### 1. `src/config/mod.rs` — add `repeat_interval` to `MitosisConfig`

Add field:
```rust
/// Re-run mitosis every N consecutive failures after the first (0 = disabled).
/// Fires at failure_count == 1, 1+N, 1+2N, ...
/// Only when force_failure_threshold == 0.
/// Beads already carrying a mitosis-depth label are skipped.
#[serde(default)]
pub repeat_interval: u32,
```

### 2. `src/mitosis/mod.rs` — update failure-count gate

In the `else if self.config.first_failure_only && failure_count != 1` branch, extend to
also allow firing when `repeat_interval > 0` and `(failure_count - 1) % repeat_interval == 0`
AND the bead does not have a `mitosis-depth:*` label. Keep the existing early-return pattern.

### 3. Unit tests in `src/mitosis/mod.rs`

- `repeat_interval_triggers_at_correct_counts`: fires at 1, 1+N, 1+2N; skips all others
- `repeat_interval_skips_max_depth_beads`: bead with `mitosis-depth:1` label + repeat tick → skipped
- `repeat_interval_zero_preserves_first_failure_only`: interval=0, first_failure_only=true → only fires at 1

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo fmt` + `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- All existing mitosis tests pass
- New unit tests pass
- Config `[mitosis]\nrepeat_interval = 50` causes re-split at failure 51, 101, etc.

title: Investigate: ~100+ claude processes leaked at cwd=$HOME for 11-13h, saturated lab to load 300+
description:
Observed 2026-07-29 ~13:35 EDT on lab (100.81.129.38): load average 304-308 on a 12-core box (worse than any prior recorded fleet incident, including the 07-28 17-pinned-worker crisis that peaked at load 200+). vmstat confirmed it was real, not cosmetic: procs.r (runnable) was 281-295, %sy (kernel time) pegged at 100%, %us at 0% — pure context-switch thrashing (70-100k switches/sec), not actual work. Memory/swap were fine (34/62Gi used, 254Mi swap) — ruled out memory pressure as the driver.

Root cause of the load: found via `ps -eo comm --no-headers | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` — 115 separate 'claude' processes, vastly more than the 4 live 'needle run' supervisors present at the time, and far beyond any previously recorded fleet size. Per-process inspection (`readlink /proc/<pid>/cwd`) showed EVERY one of the 115 had cwd = /home/coding — the bare home directory, not any project repo/workspace. Elapsed times ranged 41735-48134s (11.6-13.4h), clustered into groups sharing identical spawn timestamps (consistent with programmatic mass-spawn over time, not 115 separate manual terminal sessions). All 115 shared PPID = the tmux server hosting the needle-supervisor session (normal tmux pane-reparenting, not itself meaningful).

IMPORTANT — this is distinct from bf-12bim (supervisor zombie/defunct-child non-reaping, GH #12): these were LIVE, RUNNING processes, not <defunct> zombies. Proof: `pkill -9 -x claude` successfully killed all of them immediately (zombies are already dead and cannot be re-killed) — pgrep -c -x claude went to 0/1, then within seconds needle supervise's autoscaler correctly spun up 3 fresh workers with correct cwd (~/claude-print, ~/miroir, ~/drawrace), confirming the supervisor's spawn/autoscale logic itself is healthy. run-queue and load recovered immediately (vmstat procs.r dropped to 1-3, idle% to 82%, free memory 4.7Gi -> 24Gi).

NOT YET ROOT-CAUSED — open research questions for whoever picks this up:
1. What code path spawns a 'claude' process with cwd left at the operator's home directory instead of cd'ing into the target workspace first? Check src/dispatch/mod.rs (run_process) and src/supervisor/mod.rs (spawn_worker) for any fallback/default path taken when workspace resolution fails, is empty, or a workspace arg is omitted — does it silently fall back to the process's inherited cwd instead of erroring?
2. Why did ~115 of these accumulate over ~11-13h without anything reaping/killing them? Is there a retry loop that spawns a new claude on every tick without checking/killing the previous attempt if it hasn't exited? Cross-check against bf-1ynu9 (supervisor spawns workers via current_exe() instead of PATH lookup) and bf-12bim (zombie reaping) for any shared code path, though neither obviously explains a home-dir cwd.
3. What were these processes actually doing/blocked on for 11+ hours? If any `~/.needle/logs/needle-*.stderr.log` or claude-side transcript/session logs exist for PIDs active in the 2026-07-29 ~00:48-13:35 EDT window, check whether they show a real dispatch attempt that hung (e.g. waiting on stdin, a broken PTY, a network call that never returns) versus something spawned outside the normal dispatch path entirely (health check, canary, some other subprocess call to the 'claude' binary).
4. Is this reproducible on demand, or was it a one-off (e.g. triggered by one of the 07-28 fleet collapse/relaunch cycles leaving these behind)? Check whether the same pattern (claude count wildly disproportionate to needle process count, cwd=$HOME) recurs after future collapses/relaunches.

Fingerprint to grep for if this recurs: `ps -eo comm | sort | uniq -c` showing claude count >> needle process count, combined with `/proc/<pid>/cwd` resolving to the operator home directory across the cluster, and elapsed times all much older than any live needle process's uptime.

title: Config paths with literal ~ are not tilde-expanded — creates literal ./~/ dir in workspace
description:
## Problem
A literal directory named '~' exists at the repo root (see ~/.needle/state/heartbeats, ~/.needle/state/workers.json, pulse/reflect/weave state under it — all relative to the workspace root, i.e. a directory literally named tilde). Cause: the 'needle init' config template (src/cli/mod.rs, ~line 1293) writes 'home: ~/.needle' under 'workspace:', and the config loader (src/config/mod.rs) never expands a leading '~/' in path-typed config values — grep confirms no tilde/expand logic exists. YAML '~/.needle' therefore becomes a relative path, so every worker creates a literal '~' tree in its cwd. Built-in defaults use dirs_or_home() (src/config/mod.rs ~line 2153) which reads HOME correctly, so only file/env-provided paths are affected.

## Impact
Heartbeat files, worker registry, and strand state land in per-cwd literal '~' dirs instead of the real HOME, silently breaking peer heartbeat visibility, stale-claim cleanup, and splice detection across workers with different cwds. Relates to plan.md 'Concurrency > Heartbeat Protocol' (heartbeat_dir default ~/.needle/state/heartbeats/) and 'Configuration' chapter.

## Fix
1. Add tilde expansion (leading '~/' -> HOME) applied uniformly to all path-typed config fields on load (workspace.home, heartbeat_dir, adapters_dir, canary_workspace, telemetry paths, etc.) in src/config/mod.rs.
2. Keep 'needle init' template as-is (now safe) or switch it to write the absolute path.
3. 'needle doctor' should warn when a literal './~' directory exists in the workspace.
4. Delete the stray literal '~' directory from the NEEDLE repo root (it is untracked) and add '~/' to .gitignore as a guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests: '~/.needle' in global config, workspace .needle.yaml, and env var all resolve under HOME; bare '~' and '~/x' handled; paths without tilde unchanged; missing HOME falls back sanely.
- Running a worker from any cwd with the init-generated config creates state under HOME, never a literal ./~/.
- needle doctor flags an existing literal ./~ dir.
- cargo clippy clean; no unwrap/expect in non-test code.

```rust
let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().context("failed to create tokio runtime")?;

```

description:
Discovered 2026-07-28 while adding tests for bf-3pc1r/bf-j8o7w (GH #8/#9, commit e97e88a). CommandGate::run_command (src/validation/mod.rs) calls the fully synchronous, blocking std::process::Command::output() with no .await point during a gate command's execution. tokio::time::timeout's Timeout::poll polls the wrapped future first and only checks its deadline if that poll returns Pending -- so a wrapped future with no yield point during a slow blocking segment always completes before the deadline check can matter.

Net effect: validation.outcome_timeout_seconds (now configurable per GH #8) can only observe, after the fact, that a gate command ran longer than the configured timeout -- it cannot actually cut the command off mid-execution the way its role (outcome-handler gate timeout) implies. A gate command that hangs or runs very long will block the whole outcome-handling task for its full duration regardless of the configured timeout value.

First discovered via a broken test: an initial version of a handle_with_cancellation test used a slow verification: gate command (sleep 2) to try to trigger a 1s configured timeout, and it failed on iad-ci (workflow needle-ci-g7cqh) because the gate ran to completion (2s) before the timeout could ever be observed. The test was corrected (commit 4d8820f) to use a genuinely-async slow store operation instead, which does correctly demonstrate the config value is honored for the *other* (already-async) operations handle() performs -- just not for gate command execution itself.

Suggested fix: run CommandGate's std::process::Command::output() inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking, so the returned JoinHandle future is a genuine yield point tokio::time::timeout can race against. The underlying OS process would still need its own kill-on-timeout handling (spawn_blocking alone doesn't kill the child process if the JoinHandle is abandoned) to avoid leaking a runaway subprocess after the outer timeout fires -- worth designing deliberately rather than bolting on.

Acceptance criteria: a gate command configured to run longer than validation.outcome_timeout_seconds is actually interrupted (its OS process killed, not just outlived) at approximately the configured timeout, with a regression test proving it (a slow gate command + short configured timeout observed to return around the timeout, not after the full command duration).
close_reason: Fixed: Gate::validate is now async (#[async_trait]); CommandGate uses tokio::process::Command with kill_on_drop(true) instead of blocking std::process::Command. A slow gate command is now a genuine yield point tokio::time::timeout can actually abandon and kill, not just report late. Verified with command_gate_slow_command_is_killed_when_dropped_mid_flight and handle_with_cancellation_kills_a_slow_verification_gate_command (end-to-end repro of the original scenario). 405 targeted tests pass. See ADR-009 addendum, plan.md 13.6a.

description:
`ExploreConfig::default()` is `workspaces: []` (auto-discover) plus
`workspace_root` from `default_workspace_root()` -> `dirs_or_home("")`, i.e. the
real home directory. Any test that builds a `Worker` **in-process** inherits
this and scans every directory under $HOME containing a `.beads/`, claiming REAL
beads from REAL repos under the fixture adapter/worker identity.

The "Test Isolation Policy" in CLAUDE.md (from the 2026-07-20 incident, ADR-006)
covers only tests that spawn the needle BINARY and isolate via
`cmd.env("HOME", ...)`. Setting HOME affects child processes only, so
in-process workers fall straight through the gap.

## Impact (2026-08-05)

An orphaned local `integration_tests` binary roamed into bead-forge, set beads
to `in_progress` under assignee `echo-test-test-worker` (adapter `echo-test` +
worker `test-worker`), and a full export from the emptied db truncated
bead-forge's `.beads/issues.jsonl` to 0 bytes. 2302 beads recovered from git.

## Done

- `tests/integration_tests.rs` `test_config()` now pins
  `strands.explore.workspace_root` to the temp home and clears `workspaces`.
- CLAUDE.md gained an in-process clause under Test Isolation Policy.

## Remaining

- Six other test files build `Config::default()` without pinning explore:
  `heartbeat_validation.rs`, `sigterm_heartbeat_cleanup.rs`,
  `otlp_integration.rs`, `p3_integration_tests.rs` and others. Audit which
  actually start a worker loop that can reach Explore.
- Add a guard test that fails when a test constructs `Config::default()`
  without pinning `strands.explore`. bead-forge has an equivalent at
  `tests/workspace_isolation_guard.rs`.
- Consider making the unsafe combination impossible by construction rather
  than by convention.

title: fix(worker): unbounded tracing span nesting on claim path floods stderr at ~159 GB/hr
description:
## Symptom

A single worker's stderr log grew to 33.7 GB and was still growing at ~159 GB/hr
when killed. On lab (2026-08-05) this consumed 33 GB of a 444 GB disk in under
30 minutes and was ~50 minutes from filling the root filesystem.

Observed on worker `claude-print-opus-alpha`, workspace `cgov-polish-queue`,
needle 0.2.15.

## Evidence

Each log line carries its full tracing span stack, and the stack never unwinds:

    worker.session{...}:bead.claim{...}:bead.lifecycle{...}:bead.claim{...}:bead.lifecycle{...}...

Measured within one session, same event type:

| sample | bead.claim depth | bead.lifecycle depth | longest line |
|--------|------------------|----------------------|--------------|
| early  | 18               | 18                   | 4,983 bytes  |
| late   | 2,488            | 2,488                | 629,829 bytes |

The two depths are exactly equal, and grow by one pair per claim cycle. Because
every subsequent event re-serializes the whole accumulated stack, total output
grows quadratically — which is why the rate was unremarkable at first and
reached 159 GB/hr about 20 minutes in.

## Root cause

`src/worker/mod.rs:1608`

    self.bead_lifecycle_span = Some(lifecycle_span.entered());

`EnteredSpan` is a RAII guard over the thread-local span stack, which requires
LIFO drop order. On the next claim this line evaluates in the wrong order:

1. `lifecycle_span.entered()` pushes the NEW span onto the stack
2. the assignment then drops the OLD `EnteredSpan`, popping it

The old guard is no longer on top when it drops, so the exit is out of order and
the previous span is never removed. One `bead.lifecycle` leaks per claim cycle.

The same defect hits `bead.claim` at `src/worker/mod.rs:1552`:

    let _claim_enter = claim_span.enter();

`_claim_enter` is dropped at end of scope, i.e. AFTER line 1608 has already
pushed the lifecycle span on top of it — again out of order. This is why
`bead.claim` and `bead.lifecycle` accumulate at identical depth.

The comment at `src/worker/mod.rs:1610` asserts the claim span "is dropped here",
which is not what the code does.

## Deliverables

- Fix the guard ordering so each claim cycle exits its spans LIFO. Options:
  explicitly drop the previous `bead_lifecycle_span` before entering the new one;
  drop `_claim_enter` before line 1608; or stop holding `EnteredSpan` across
  await points / in struct fields and use `Span` + `.in_scope()` / `Instrument`.
- Note: holding an `EnteredSpan` across an `.await` (line 1560) is itself unsound
  for async and is worth removing regardless.
- Add a bound / guard so a runaway span stack can never again produce
  multi-hundred-KB log lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker running >=200 consecutive claim cycles shows constant span depth in
  stderr — not monotonically increasing.
- Regression test asserts span depth after N claims is O(1), not O(N).
- Max observed log line length stays bounded across a long run.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt` clean.

## Repro / artifacts

Samples preserved on lab at `.needle/logs/samples/alpha-stderr-{head,tail}-2MB.log`
(relative to the coding user's home). The head sample shows depth 18, the tail
sample depth 2,488, same session `d5813a0d`.
notes: Implemented and pushed commit a34974f: replaced cross-await EnteredSpan guards with async instrumentation, stored bead.lifecycle as Span, added a 64 KiB tracing line cap for file/stderr writers, and added a 200-cycle depth/line regression. Targeted regressions, log-writer tests, mitosis/knot tests, modified-file rustfmt, and cargo clippy --lib --bins -- -D warnings pass. Local cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings reaches a pre-existing clippy::zombie_processes failure in tests/process_discovery_integration.rs:127. Authoritative workflow needle-ci-t7vzh cannot start verification: PVC needle-ci-t7vzh-workspace requests 2Gi with storage class ssd, while the Rackspace provisioner requires 5-20Gi; workflow remains Pending/Unschedulable and prior needle-ci-6d5d5 is stuck on the same condition. Per repository policy, leaving bead open until CI infrastructure is repaired and a workflow succeeds.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTION (verified against tracing-subscriber 0.3.23 source). The stated mechanism -- non-LIFO exit leaving the previous span un-popped -- does not hold. SpanStack::pop does a reverse search and stack.remove(idx), so it removes the span from anywhere in the stack, not just the top; an out-of-order exit on a single thread is harmless. The mechanism that actually leaks is the one noted only in passing at the end of the bead: holding the EnteredSpan across .await. On a multi-thread runtime the task resumes on another thread, the guard drops there, that stack has no matching id, pop() returns false, and the original thread's entry is orphaned. Fixed in c2d83c3 by switching to .instrument(). Note for auditing other enter() call sites: the rule is 'never hold a guard across await', not 'preserve LIFO order'.

title: Wire GitHub-release upgrade path into canary-gated :testing channel (ADR-005)
description:
Implements ADR-005 in docs/adr/ (005-unify...) referenced from plan.md Phase 9.

Today perform_upgrade() (src/upgrade/mod.rs) downloads a new GitHub release and overwrites
env::current_exe() directly, with zero canary validation and zero fleet propagation. Separately,
check_auto_canary()/check_hot_reload() in src/worker/mod.rs already implement a full, tested,
canary-gated hot-reload pipeline that runs every worker-loop cycle -- but it only ever reacts to
a needle-testing binary written by the (disabled) self-modification pipeline. Nothing connects
"new GitHub release" to that channel. Live-confirmed drift during 2026-07-20 audit: ex44's
installed needle reported 0.2.11 while GitHub's latest release was v0.2.12, published the same day.

Deliverables:
1. New function alongside check_for_update() (src/upgrade/mod.rs) that downloads a newer release
   to needle_home/bin/needle-testing instead of overwriting the running binary. Skip (log why) if
   a :testing binary is already present and unpromoted, so this can't clobber an in-flight
   self-modification candidate.
2. Periodic poll in needle supervise (src/supervisor/mod.rs) calling that function on interval
   supervisor.update_check_interval_secs (default 21600), gated behind new
   supervisor.auto_upgrade_check: bool (default false).
3. No changes needed to check_auto_canary()/check_hot_reload() -- verify via test that a
   release-sourced :testing binary is picked up identically to a self-modification-sourced one.
4. Regression tests per plan.md Phase 9.4.

Acceptance criteria: with auto_upgrade_check=true and a mocked newer release, a full poll cycle
produces a promoted :stable and a subsequent hot-reload in worker-loop tests; a failing canary
leaves :stable untouched; needle upgrade (manual path) is unchanged.

title: needle-ci publishes DRAFT releases, so 'needle upgrade' has been stuck on v0.2.12 since 2026-07-29
description:
Found 2026-08-02 while releasing v0.2.16.

Every release the needle-ci WorkflowTemplate has produced since v0.2.13 is a
GitHub *draft*:

  v0.2.16  draft=true  assets=6
  v0.2.15  draft=true  assets=6
  v0.2.14  draft=true  assets=6
  v0.2.13  draft=true  assets=6
  v0.2.12  draft=false  <- last published one, 2026-07-20

Drafts are invisible to the releases/latest API, so
GET /repos/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest returned v0.2.12 and
'needle upgrade --check' failed outright with:

  https://api.github.com/repos/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest: status code 404

Impact: the sanctioned upgrade path has been dead for four releases and ~5
weeks. No host could auto-upgrade past 0.2.12; ex44 and bench were both sitting
on 0.2.14. Because the binaries were still attached to the drafts, the failure
looked like 'the release exists but upgrade is broken' rather than 'the release
was never published'.

The template at k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml does NOT
pass --draft, so gh is producing drafts on its own. Most likely cause is the
GitHub App installation token (the credential helper sets
username=x-access-token) lacking the permission gh needs to publish, so it
degrades to a draft rather than erroring.

Worked around for v0.2.16 only, by hand:
  gh release edit v0.2.16 --repo jedarden/NEEDLE --draft=false --latest

Fix direction: make the release step explicit and fail loudly — add --latest to
the gh release create call and then assert the result is published (query
releases/latest and compare the tag), so a silent degradation to draft breaks
CI instead of shipping a release nobody can install. Also decide whether
v0.2.13-v0.2.15 should be published retroactively or left as drafts.

Acceptance: a needle-ci run leaves a published, non-draft release that
'needle upgrade --check' can see, and the workflow fails if it does not.

title: Verify test fails with expected panic before fix
description:
## Scope
Confirm that the test FAILS with the expected tokio runtime panic before the fix from bf-3s2b0 is applied.

## What to do
1. Build and run the test
2. Confirm it panics with tokio runtime error
3. Capture the exact panic message
4. Document the failure mode

## Acceptance criteria
- Test runs and panics as expected
- Panic message mentions tokio runtime
- Failure is documented in bead comments
- Test is in known-bad state before fix

## Expected failure
Should panic with something like "cannot be called from outside of a Tokio 1.x runtime"
notes:
✅ VERIFIED: Test successfully demonstrates tokio runtime panic before fix

**Test executed:** 

**Exact panic message captured:**
'there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime'

**Stack trace shows:**
- tokio::task::spawn::spawn() at tokio-1.53.1/src/task/spawn.rs:183:13
- Triggered at tests/otlp_runtime_test.rs:37:9

**Test behavior:**
- Test correctly catches the panic via std::panic::catch_unwind()
- Asserts that result.is_err() - confirming the spawn failed
- Test PASSES (meaning the panic was successfully verified)

**Failure mode documented:**
Without rt.enter(), tokio::spawn cannot find a reactor context in the current thread and panics immediately. This is the exact bug pattern from bf-3s2b0 where init_tracing_subscriber was called without an entered runtime guard.

**Test location:** tests/otlp_runtime_test.rs:22-49

All acceptance criteria met. Test is in known-bad state before fix is applied.
close_reason: ✅ Successfully verified test demonstrates expected tokio runtime panic before fix. Test 'test_tokio_spawn_panics_without_entered_runtime' correctly panics with message 'there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime'. Panic caught via std::panic::catch_unwind() and verified with assert!(result.is_err()). Test is in known-bad state confirming the bug pattern from bf-3s2b0.

title: Unbind BrCliBeadStore from the bf binary — its argv is correct beads_rust, discover() resolves bf first
description:
src/bead_store/mod.rs:1550-1563 builds `create --title T --body B --json --silent [--labels a,b]`. bf 0.4.1 create accepts NONE of --body, --silent, --labels — only --title --description --type --priority --assignee --label (repeated) --json --envelope --no-auto-flush --no-progress --workspace. Verified via `bf create --help` on 2026-08-11.

BrCliBeadStore is the store EVERY worker path uses (worker/mod.rs:1385, supervisor/mod.rs:214, strand/explore.rs:71/:450, strand/splice.rs:747/:839/:999) and its discover() resolves `bf` FIRST — so the fleet runs the old br dialect against a binary that rejects it. BfCliBeadStore::create_bead (:2267-2280) already does it correctly but is only constructed in cli/mod.rs:997/:3384.

Blast radius: create_bead fails with a clap parse error (exit 2), and through the trait default split_bead (:646-668) that takes ALL mitosis child creation with it.

Deliverables:
- BrCliBeadStore::create_bead emits `--description` and repeated `--label`, matching BfCliBeadStore.
- Drop --json/--silent; bf create prints the bare ID on stdout already (the existing stdout.trim() parse is correct).
- A fixture-CLI test asserting the exact argv, so this cannot regress silently.

Acceptance criteria:
- Argv assertion test passes for create_bead with 0, 1, and 2 labels.
- fmt + clippy + full test suite green on iad-ci.
- Sequenced BEFORE the bead_store module split so the two do not collide in the same file.

See docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md, Addendum.
close_reason: Fixed BrCliBeadStore::create_bead to use bf 0.4.1+ CLI dialect (--description, repeated --label) instead of legacy br dialect (--body, --silent, comma-separated --labels). Also fixed add_dependency to use --blocks instead of --type blocks. All argv assertion tests pass (0, 1, 2, 3 labels), fmt + clippy green, commit a9d3e11 pushed to main.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-11 — THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION PRESCRIBES THE WRONG FIX. DO NOT rewrite --body to --description in this store.

The real beads_rust binary is ~/.cargo/bin/br v0.1.28 (dicklesworthstone/beads_rust). ~/.local/bin/br is a SHIM that execs bf, so `which br` does not find it — which is how this went unnoticed.

Probed against real br 0.1.28:
- create -d/--description [aliases: --body] — --body IS VALID
- --silent — VALID
- -l/--labels comma-separated — VALID
- dep add <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> -t blocks — TWO positionals, VALID

So BrCliBeadStore::create_bead (:1550-1563) and add_dependency (:1579) are CORRECT beads_rust. Nothing about their argv is stale.

The actual defect is BrCliBeadStore::discover (:758-775): it resolves bf BEFORE br, binding the beads_rust adapter to the bead-forge binary, which rejects that argv. Compounding it, bf-only calls were grafted into this store — claim (:1428-1437), release (:1479-1486), split (:1485/:1508) via bf batch, and claim_auto via bf claim (:1194-1220) — using the second resolver at :1127. beads_rust has NEITHER subcommand.

REVISED DELIVERABLES:
- Do NOT touch create_bead or add_dependency argv in this store.
- Make BrCliBeadStore resolve br only, and confirm it is real beads_rust, not the shim (the shim execs bf and will silently pass a --version check).
- Remove the grafted bf batch/claim paths and the :1127 resolver from this store; claim/release/clear_assignee use update -s <status> --assignee ..., which beads_rust has.
- claim_auto: beads_rust has no claim subcommand — implement as non-atomic ready then claim(id), and LOG the downgrade (real TOCTOU window, matters for multi-worker fleets).
- Argv assertion tests pinned to real br 0.1.28 help output.

The one genuine argv bug is in the OTHER store: BfCliBeadStore::add_dependency (:2288) sends two positionals; bf 0.4.1 takes one (<BLOCKER> --blocks <BLOCKED>). Tracked on bf-s5hb8, now narrowed to the bf store only.

See docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md section 5 and Revision History.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
SCOPE NOTE 2026-08-11 (ADR-013 draft 3) — this bead survives as the INTERIM tactical fix. Keep it narrow.

The final design deletes BrCliBeadStore entirely and replaces both stores with one descriptor-driven CliBeadStore (bf-1awps). That work is ~6 beads deep and gated behind the descriptor type, the strategy set, and the engine. Meanwhile the chimera is breaking mitosis child creation on every fleet host TODAY.

So: do the minimal unbinding here, do NOT start the descriptor refactor from this bead.

Minimal interim fix:
- BrCliBeadStore resolves br ONLY, and verifies it is real beads_rust (~/.cargo/bin/br v0.1.28), not the ~/.local/bin/br shim that execs bf.
- Still do NOT rewrite create_bead or add_dependency argv — they are correct beads_rust (see comment 1).
- De-grafting the bf batch/claim paths is tracked separately and folds into the beads_rust descriptor (bf-4e92i); do not do it here unless it is required to make the unbinding compile.

When the descriptor engine lands, this code is deleted wholesale — so favor the smallest change that stops the fleet sending beads_rust argv to the bf binary, not a clean-up of code with a known expiry date.

See docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md Decision and Revision History.

title: Verify NEEDLE OTLP telemetry emits correctly end-to-end (post-crash-fix)
description:
## Purpose

bf-4icyq fixes the startup crash so a worker with `otlp_sink.enabled: true`
can boot at all. That only proves it doesn't crash — it does not prove the
telemetry it emits is correct, complete, or actually reaches any consumer.
This bead is the follow-on: verify the signal itself, end-to-end, across
every hop and every consumer.

Blocked on bf-4icyq (can't meaningfully test emission until the worker can
stay up).

## What NEEDLE actually emits (confirmed by reading src/telemetry/otlp.rs)

- **Logs**: `emit_log()` fires for every single TelemetryEvent, unconditionally
  — attributes `event_type`, `worker_id`, `session_id`, `sequence`, optional
  `bead_id`, JSON-string body. This is the complete event stream.
- **Metrics**: only specific event types map to instruments (see
  `dispatch_event`'s match arms). Confirmed instrument names as currently
  implemented: `needle.workers.active`, `needle.beads.claimed`,
  `needle.beads.completed`, `needle.beads.duration`, `needle.claim.attempts`,
  `needle.strand.duration`, `needle.agent.duration`,
  `needle.agent.tokens.input`, `needle.agent.tokens.output`,
  `needle.cost.usd`, `needle.heartbeat.age`, `needle.queue.depth`,
  `needle.peers.stale`, `needle.mitosis.children_created`. Export cadence is
  `PeriodicReader` on `config.telemetry.otlp_sink.metrics_interval_secs`
  (10s in ex44's current config).
- **Traces**: a tracer/span pipeline exists (`build_grpc_providers` /
  `build_http_providers` both construct a `SdkTracerProvider`), but
  `dispatch_event` only explicitly emits span *events* for
  `heartbeat.emitted`/`build.heartbeat` via `emit_span_event`. Confirm during
  testing whether any real spans (not just span events) are actually
  produced, since the doc comment above `dispatch_event` claims several
  event types map to spans but the match arms mostly only touch metrics/logs.

**Known naming discrepancy to check**: FABRIC's own docs
(`FABRIC/docs/needle-exporter-wiring.md`) describe NEEDLE emitting
`needle.worker.tokens.in`, `needle.worker.tokens.out`, `needle.worker.cost.usd`,
`needle.worker.beads.completed/failed`, `needle.worker.errors`,
`needle.bead.duration` — this does **not** match the instrument names
actually in `otlp.rs` today (listed above). Either FABRIC's doc is stale
against an older NEEDLE version, or there's a real mismatch that would
silently break FABRIC's `INSTRUMENT_ALIASES` resolution and any Grafana
dashboard built against the documented names. Resolve which is true before
building anything downstream that depends on specific metric names.

## Test plan

### 1. Synthetic collector smoke test (no NEEDLE involved — isolates the collector/auth path)

```bash
curl -X POST http://needle-otel-ex44-apexalgo-iad-ts.ardenone.com:4318/v1/logs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $EX44_OTLP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resourceLogs":[{"resource":{"attributes":[{"key":"service.name","value":{"stringValue":"needle"}}]},"scopeLogs":[{"scope":{"name":"needle"},"logRecords":[{"timeUnixNano":"<now-ns>","body":{"stringValue":"{}"},"attributes":[{"key":"event_type","value":{"stringValue":"test.smoke"}},{"key":"worker_id","value":{"stringValue":"smoke-test"}}]}]}]}]}'
```

Confirms auth + routing works before trusting anything from a real worker.
A 200 with empty body `{}` (or `{"partialSuccess":{}}`) is success.

### 2. Collector self-metrics (confirms the collector actually received + forwarded, independent of NEEDLE or downstream stores)

The collector exposes its own Prometheus metrics on `:8888`
(`needle-otel-collector.needle-observability.svc.cluster.local:8888/metrics`,
cluster-internal only). After step 1 and again after a real worker run, check:

- `otelcol_receiver_accepted_log_records{receiver="otlp/ex44"}` — increments
- `otelcol_receiver_accepted_metric_points{receiver="otlp/ex44"}` — increments once a worker emits metrics
- `otelcol_exporter_sent_log_records{exporter="otlphttp/victorialogs"}` and `{exporter="otlphttp/dashboard"}` — both should increment together; if only one does, the fan-out is broken for the other
- `otelcol_exporter_sent_metric_points{exporter="prometheusremotewrite"}` — will be 0/failing until the apex Prometheus disk-full issue (found 2026-08-08, separate from this bead) is resolved — do not treat that as an OTLP bug
- Watch for `otelcol_exporter_send_failed_*` counters on any exporter — nonzero means silent drops downstream of the collector

### 3. Real worker test on ex44 (after bf-4icyq lands and needle-stable is rebuilt/deployed)

```bash
# Launch with an explicit, clearly-labeled identifier so its telemetry is easy to find downstream
tmux new-session -d -s needle-claude-code-glm47-otel-verify \
  "NEEDLE_INNER=1 /home/coding/.needle/bin/needle-stable run --workspace /home/coding/NEEDLE --agent claude-code-glm47 --count 1 --identifier otel-verify --timeout 1200 2>> /home/coding/.needle/logs/needle-claude-code-glm47-otel-verify.stderr.log"
```

- Confirm the process stays up (no panic) — this is bf-4icyq's own criterion, re-checked here as a gate before continuing.
- `grep -i "otlp\|export failed" .needle/logs/needle-claude-code-glm47-otel-verify.stderr.log` — should show no `OTLP log export failed` / `OTLP tracing layer export failure` WARN lines. If present, that's the auth/token question from bf-4icyq's parent investigation resurfacing — capture the exact error text, it will say why (401 vs timeout vs TLS).
- Let it run long enough to emit at least one full cycle: a claim attempt, a heartbeat (30s interval per `health.heartbeat_interval_secs`), and ideally one full bead completion — each exercises a different instrument/log path.

### 4. Logs path — VictoriaLogs + dashboard.ardenone.com/needle

- Query VictoriaLogs directly for the `otel-verify` worker's stream and confirm records with `event_type`/`worker_id`/`bead_id` attributes are present and match what the worker actually did (cross-check a few against the raw JSONL in `~/.needle/logs/` for the same worker — same events should appear in both, this is the dual-ingestion path FABRIC's doc describes).
- Hit `https://dashboard.ardenone.com/needle/api/dashboard` (authenticated) and confirm:
  - `environments.ex44.active_workers` reflects the new worker while it's active
  - `workers[]` contains an entry with `worker_id` containing `otel-verify`, correct `state`, and `last_seen` advancing
  - `events[]` contains real event types, not just heartbeats
- Open the actual page and confirm the SSE `/stream` pushes updates live (not just on manual reload) — watch the `#connection` badge go to "Live", and watch a row update in real time when the worker transitions state.

### 5. Metrics path — apex Prometheus / Grafana (blocked until the disk-full Prometheus issue is separately fixed)

- Once Prometheus is healthy again, query for the actual instrument names confirmed in the "what NEEDLE emits" section above (not the FABRIC-doc names, unless step 0 above resolves the discrepancy in FABRIC's favor) — e.g. `needle_beads_claimed_total{deployment_cluster="ex44"}`.
- Confirm `deployment.cluster`/`telemetry.source`/`fleet.name` attributes were correctly overwritten by the collector's `resource/ex44` processor (README says client-supplied values for these three are not trusted — verify the enforcement actually happens, don't just assume the config does what the README says).
- Confirm `needle.worker.pool` (client-supplied, not overwritten) survived intact.

### 6. Cleanup

Stop the `otel-verify` worker (`tmux kill-session -t needle-claude-code-glm47-otel-verify`) once verification is complete — it's a diagnostic worker, not meant to run indefinitely.

## Acceptance criteria

- Synthetic smoke test (step 1) succeeds independent of any real worker.
- Collector self-metrics (step 2) confirm accept + forward counts increment for both the VictoriaLogs and dashboard exporters.
- A real worker (step 3) runs for at least one full bead lifecycle with zero `OTLP ... export failed` warnings in its own log.
- At least one real event from that worker is independently confirmed in VictoriaLogs, in the raw JSONL, AND on `dashboard.ardenone.com/needle` (all three, not just one).
- The FABRIC-doc-vs-otlp.rs instrument-name discrepancy is resolved (doc fixed, or code fixed, whichever is stale) and documented.
- Findings (pass/fail per step, any error text captured) are added back to this bead before closing.

title: needle stop --all help claims it stops workers; it only kills tmux sessions and orphans supervisors
description:
Companion to bf-4iwog (which covers `needle run --workspace`). This bead covers
the remaining help-text accuracy gaps, with `stop` as the serious one.

1. `needle stop --all` — CURRENTLY WRONG, and it matters

   Help says:   --all    Stop all needle workers

   Observed 2026-08-07 stopping a 17-worker fleet: `needle stop --all` killed the
   tmux sessions (the tmux server itself went away) but every supervisor survived,
   reparented to init:

     pid=1287492 state=S ppid=1 elapsed=05:31 children=2 --identifier alpha
     ... 8 identical

   They then ignored SIGINT entirely — both the supervisors and their children —
   while stuck in the pre-dispatch shell. Only SIGKILL cleared them. The command
   also printed its own contradiction:

     "kill attempt reported success but 3 process(es) still running"

   An operator reading the help concludes the fleet is stopped. It is not: the
   supervisors keep running, keep their claims, and can keep dispatching. This is
   the difference between "the fleet is down" and "the fleet looks down", and it
   is exactly the state you must NOT be in before rewriting git history or doing
   anything else that assumes quiescence.

   Suggested wording:

     --all
         Kill the tmux session of every registered worker.
         This does NOT reliably terminate the worker supervisors: a
         `needle run` process whose session is killed is commonly reparented
         to init and keeps running, and may ignore SIGINT. After this
         command, verify with `pgrep -af needle-stable run` and signal any
         survivors directly. See `needle cleanup` for session hygiene.

2. `needle supervise --workspace` — same ambiguity as bf-4iwog

   Help says:  Workspace to monitor (defaults to config workspace)
   Unclear whether the supervisor scales workers for that one workspace only, or
   uses it as a home while auto-discovery applies. Should state which.

3. `needle cleanup` is the model to copy — no change needed

   Its help already spells out exactly what the destructive flag does and when to
   use the safe form. The other subcommands should match that standard. Worth
   noting so nobody "fixes" it.

Acceptance: `needle stop --help` states that supervisors may survive and tells
the operator how to verify; `needle supervise --help` disambiguates scope.

NOTE: filed rather than hand-edited because a worker was EXECUTING in this repo
at filing time.

title: 16.4a Author the beads_rust builtin descriptor (no claim, no batch)
description:
BrCliBeadStore is currently a chimera: beads_rust argv for create/dep/sync/list, but bead-forge argv for claim/release/split, bound to whichever binary discover() finds first.

bf-only code grafted into the beads_rust store:
- :1194-1220 claim_auto -> `bf claim --model/--harness/--harness-version --assignee --json`
- :1428-1437 claim -> `bf batch --json [{op:update,...}]`
- :1479-1486 release -> `bf batch`
- :1485/:1508 split_bead -> `bf batch`
- :1127-1136 a second, independent resolve_bf() serving only the above

beads_rust 0.1.28 has NEITHER `claim` NOR `batch` (verified: `br claim` -> "unrecognized subcommand", `br batch` -> "unrecognized subcommand"). It DOES have `update -s/--status --assignee` and a first-class `ready --json --limit`.

Deliverables:
- claim / release / clear_assignee use `update -s <status> --assignee ...` on the br binary. beads_rust never dropped --assignee, so no batch emulation is needed.
- claim_auto: no server-side claim exists. Implement as ready -> claim(id) and LOG the downgrade explicitly.
- split_bead: drop the override, inherit the non-atomic trait default (:646-668).
- Delete resolve_bf() at :1127 and run_bf_batch/run_bf_claim from this store.

Acceptance criteria:
- `grep -n "bf batch\|bf claim\|resolve_bf" src/bead_store/br_cli.rs` returns nothing.
- The TOCTOU window in the non-atomic claim_auto is documented in operator-facing docs, not only in a code comment — it changes multi-worker safety on beads_rust workspaces.
- Argv assertion tests pinned to real br 0.1.28.

See ADR-013 section 5.

both Failed. Local full --lib suite on ex44: 1711 passed / 692.81s at a 2-core cap.

for 50 percent more CPU.

  sleep of 32 seconds)
- worker::tests::default_routing_rules_anthropic_subscription_models

bug, not a logic bug. Making CI faster only widens the margin on a race; removing
the time dependence eliminates it.

#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] and drive them with tokio::time::advance
instead of real sleeps.

title: OTLP telemetry crashes worker on startup: tokio::spawn called before runtime is entered
description:
## Problem

Setting `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled: true` in config crashes every worker
immediately at startup, before it claims a bead or does anything else.
Reproduced live on ex44 2026-08-08:

```
NEEDLE worker boot: creating tokio runtime...
NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created
NEEDLE worker boot: initializing tracing subscriber...

thread 'main' (1864218) panicked at src/cli/mod.rs:826:5:
there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime
```

This is why OTLP has never actually worked fleet-wide despite the sink being
implemented and the collector/dashboard side being fully wired
(apexalgo-iad `needle-observability` collector, `dashboard.ardenone.com/needle`)
— nobody has been able to run a worker with it enabled without an instant crash.

## Root cause

`src/cli/mod.rs`:
- Line 936: `let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()...` constructs the
  runtime but does not enter it (no `rt.enter()` guard).
- Line 941: `init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?`
  runs synchronously, still outside any runtime context.
- Inside `init_tracing_subscriber` (same file, ~line 789), when
  `config.telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled` is true, line 831 calls
  `tokio::spawn(async move { ... })` to run the OTLP drop-monitor task.
  `tokio::spawn` requires an active runtime context (`Handle::current()`),
  which does not exist yet — the runtime isn't actually entered until
  `rt.block_on(...)` at line 964, well after `init_tracing_subscriber` has
  already returned (or in this case, panicked).

Classic Tokio gotcha: constructing a `Runtime` does not make it "current"
for the calling thread. You need either an `EnterGuard` from `rt.enter()`
held across the call, or the call needs to happen inside `rt.block_on(...)`.

## Fix

Hold an entered-runtime guard across the `init_tracing_subscriber` call in
`src/cli/mod.rs`, e.g.:

```rust
let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new().context("failed to create tokio runtime")?;
let _rt_guard = rt.enter();   // <-- add this; keep alive at least through init_tracing_subscriber
eprintln!("NEEDLE worker boot: tokio runtime created");
...
init_tracing_subscriber(qualified_id.clone(), session_id.clone(), &config)?;
```

Alternative: move the OTLP layer construction (including the `tokio::spawn`
drop-monitor task) inside `rt.block_on(async { ... })` instead of calling it
from the synchronous portion of `main`. The `rt.enter()` guard is the
smaller, more localized change.

Check whether the same "runtime not entered" hazard applies to any other
`tokio::spawn` call reachable from synchronous startup code before the
first `rt.block_on` — `init_tracing_subscriber` may not be the only one.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker launched with `telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled: true` boots
  successfully (no panic) and reaches its normal claim/dispatch loop.
- Add a regression test that constructs a `Runtime` without entering it,
  then calls `init_tracing_subscriber` with OTLP enabled, and asserts it
  does not panic (this must have caught the bug — write it to fail against
  the current code first, then pass after the fix).
- Live-verify on ex44: launch a real worker with OTLP enabled, confirm no
  crash, and confirm `dashboard.ardenone.com/needle` receives at least one
  event from it (this closes the loop on the whole OTLP-to-dashboard
  pipeline, not just the crash).
