title: Split needle-ci into verify and release stages; gate release on a version change
description:
needle-ci is one monolithic pod that does setup, compile, test, a release
build and a GitHub publish, on every push to main -- guarded only by an
after-the-fact "does this tag already exist" check.

So roughly 95 percent of runs pay the full release cost, including
cargo build --release with lto=true and codegen-units=1 (the slowest possible
link configuration), only to discover the version did not change.

Do, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
- stage 1 verify: fmt, clippy, cargo check as a fast fail, then the test suite
- stage 2 release: only runs when the version in Cargo.toml differs from the
  latest published tag
- keep the existing idempotent "release already exists, skip" guard as a backstop

Acceptance: a push that does not bump the version never runs cargo build
--release; a version bump still publishes exactly one release.
close_reason:
Split needle-ci into verify and release stages

The workflow now runs in two stages:
- Verify (always runs): fmt, clippy, cargo check, then test suite — no release build
- Release (conditional): only runs when Cargo.toml version differs from latest published GitHub release, does cargo build --release and GitHub publish

This avoids the expensive cargo build --release (with lto=true and codegen-units=1) on ~95% of pushes where the version hasn't changed, saving ~15+ minutes per run.

Changes committed to declarative-config and pushed to origin:
https://github.com/jedarden/declarative-config/commit/af636020

title: Decide + record ADR for concurrent same-repo worker isolation (plan §6.9 shared working directory)

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
GAP (plan-vs-artifacts): docs/plan/plan.md §6.9 (lines ~4085-4092) is the only flagged open question in the plan that is NOT resolved in code and NOT tracked by any existing bead or ADR.

EVIDENCE
- No per-worker isolation exists in src/: grep for `worktree` across src/ returns nothing. `bead.workspace` is passed through verbatim as the `{workspace}` template var into the dispatched agent process (src/dispatch/mod.rs), so every worker assigned to a repo runs its agent in the SAME working directory.
- The per-workspace claim flock (plan §6.1, ~line 219; src/claim/) guards only the CLAIMING step's `br update --claim`, NOT the EXECUTING phase. Once two workers are each dispatched into the same repo (with DISTINCT beads), their agents can run concurrent `git add`/`commit`/`reset --hard`/`checkout` in one shared tree for the full duration of both dispatches; one agent's `reset --hard`/`checkout` can discard another's uncommitted work.
- §6.6's flock protects only NEEDLE's own post-hoc Bead-Id trailer amend (src/commit_hook.rs), not the agents' concurrent work.
- Distinct from bf-1ne6u (atomic-claim duplicate-dispatch of the SAME bead) — §6.9 is the broader shared-working-directory hazard that persists even when claiming is correct and beads are distinct.
- docs/adr/ contains ADRs 001-010; none covers this. The plan explicitly states it 'should be captured as its own ADR before implementation ... a bigger design decision than the rest of Phase 6.'

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. New ADR under docs/adr/ (Context/Decision/Alternatives/Consequences) deciding between the two directions the plan names: (a) full git-worktree isolation per worker (incl. merge-back strategy + effect on commit_hook trailer injection), or (b) accept as a known constraint + add a needle-run help/docs callout that >1 worker per repo is unsafe unless beads avoid overlapping file/branch state.
2. plan.md §6.9 updated to reference the ADR and record the chosen direction (remove 'not yet decided').

title: OTLP sink config schema diverges from plan.md (tls/signals/timeout_ms unimplemented)
description:
Found 2026-08-06 during the stash audit. Three April stashes on the merged
feat/hoop-dispatch-tag branch defined OtlpTlsConfig, OtlpSignalsConfig,
OtlpProtocol and OtlpCompression as real types. What landed in main instead is a
flattened OtlpSinkConfig, and it no longer matches the schema plan.md documents.

plan.md documents this OTLP block (twice: sections at lines 1908-1925 and
2495-2510):

  telemetry:
    otlp:
      timeout_ms: 5000
      tls:
        insecure: false
        ca_file: ""
      signals:
        traces: true
        metrics: true
        logs: true

src/config/mod.rs OtlpSinkConfig actually has:
  - tls: String            <- plan documents a NESTED MAP (insecure, ca_file)
  - timeout_secs: u64      <- plan documents timeout_ms
  - (no signals field)     <- per-signal traces/metrics/logs toggles absent

Consequences:
  1. tls is the serious one. A config written per the plan supplies a YAML map
     where serde expects a String, which is a deserialization error, not a
     silent fallback.
  2. timeout_ms and signals are silently ignored. src/config/mod.rs sets
     deny_unknown_fields nowhere (grep count: 0), so unknown keys are dropped
     and the user gets the 10s default while believing they set 5s.
  3. There is no way to export traces but suppress metrics/logs, which the plan
     explicitly offers.

Not verified end-to-end: attempting to load a plan-conformant workspace
.needle.yaml produced no otlp keys AND no error, because the workspace override
path ignored the file entirely. That is a separate known issue and it also means
this misconfiguration would fail quietly rather than loudly.

Decide and then make plan and code agree:
  - either implement the documented schema (nested tls, signals, timeout_ms,
    with serde aliases so timeout_secs keeps working), or
  - amend plan.md to document the flattened schema that actually shipped.

Adding deny_unknown_fields to the telemetry config structs is worth doing either
way, so a typo in an OTLP key is a loud failure instead of a silent default.

Acceptance: a config file copied verbatim out of plan.md loads without error and
produces the values it specifies; or plan.md matches the implemented schema.

title: Canary expectations are stale (expect status 'done'), so every upgrade is rejected 0/4 on ex44
description:
Found 2026-08-02 upgrading ex44 to v0.2.16.

'needle upgrade' downloaded 0.2.16, ran canary validation, scored 0/4 and
rejected the binary. The rejection is NOT a regression in the new build — the
canary expectations under ~/.needle/canary/expected/ are dated 2026-03-21 and
have not tracked bead-forge's vocabulary since.

expected/canary-bzl.yaml (the happy-path test) asserts:

    final_status: done

bead-forge has no 'done' status. Statuses actually in use across real
workspaces are: open, in_progress, blocked, closed, completed, pending, ready.
A closed bead reports 'closed'. NEEDLE knows this — src/types/mod.rs carries the
comment "br show --json emits 'closed' for done beads. Treat as equivalent".
So canary-bzl is unsatisfiable by ANY needle binary, old or new, and the canary
gate can never pass.

The observed run looked behaviourally fine: canary-bzl closed, canary-nnw
closed, canary-8ej blocked, canary-atw in_progress. All four were still scored
as failures, so the other three expectations are likely stale in the same way
(canary-8ej wants final_status 'open' plus a 'failure-count:1' label;
canary-nnw wants 'open' for a timeout).

Impact: the upgrade path on any host with a canary workspace is permanently
blocked, and the failure presents as 'the new binary is bad' rather than 'the
test fixtures rotted'. bench has no canary workspace, so it promoted 0.2.16
straight to :stable and its workers hot-reloaded correctly — good evidence the
binary itself is fine.

Not urgent for correctness on ex44: it still has the deprecated br shim at
~/.local/bin/br, so its 0.2.14 workers' 'br close' continues to work. The cost
is that ex44 stays on old binaries.

Fix direction: refresh the four expected/*.yaml against current bead-forge
vocabulary, and add an assertion that each expected final_status is a status
bf can actually produce, so this rots loudly next time. Also surface per-test
detail — 'needle canary --status' only prints channel state, giving no clue
which expectation failed or why.

Acceptance: 'needle upgrade' on ex44 passes canary and promotes to :stable.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Fuller diagnosis 2026-08-02 — NOT a fixture-only fix. Five independent defects; the gate has almost certainly never worked.

1. NO BEAD RESET. CanaryRunner::run() has no reset/seed step — grep for reset_bead/seed/set_status in src/canary/mod.rs returns nothing. The four beads keep whatever terminal state the last run left (now: canary-bzl=closed, canary-nnw=closed, canary-8ej=blocked, canary-atw=in_progress). A worker cannot claim a closed bead, so later runs do nothing.

2. RACE. run_test() spawns `needle run --workspace ... --count 1` WITHOUT NEEDLE_INNER=1. That form detaches into tmux and returns immediately — the upgrade output prints "Started worker ... in tmux session / Attach with: tmux attach -t ...". So child.try_wait() returns exit 0 within milliseconds and get_actual_outcome() reads the bead long before any agent work. The exit code compared for Success/Failure is the launcher's, not the agent's.

3. StateMachine UNIMPLEMENTED. get_actual_outcome() hardcodes state_transitions: Vec::new() ("Not tracked in basic canary tests"). outcomes_match() does transitions.iter().all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t)); against an always-empty vec any non-empty expected list is unsatisfiable. canary-atw could only pass with zero transitions, i.e. vacuously.

4. STALE VOCABULARY. ExpectedOutcome::default_final_status() returns "done", and expected/canary-bzl.yaml asserts final_status: done. bead-forge has no 'done' status (open/in_progress/blocked/closed/completed/pending/ready). The rot is in the source default too, so omitting the field does not help.

5. USES br. get_actual_outcome() runs Command::new(&self.br_path).args(["show", id, "--json"]). On a host without the deprecated br shim the canary errors instead of validating — same root cause as bf-15tys.

Consequence: the canary cannot pass for ANY binary, which is why 'needle upgrade' on ex44 rejected v0.2.16 at 0/4. Nothing is wrong with that build — bench has no canary workspace, promoted it, and both workers hot-reloaded and now emit 'bf close'.

Real fix spans all five points plus refreshed fixtures plus a CI cycle — materially more than editing YAML. Until then the gate protects nothing; it is a permanent block that presents as "the new binary is bad".

title: cargo clippy --all-targets fails on examples/validate_p95_values.rs (blocks the clippy gate)
description:
Discovered 2026-08-06 while reviewing stashes.

cargo clippy --all-targets currently FAILS (not warns) on:

  error: this comparison involving the minimum or maximum element for this
  type contains a case that is always true or always false
    --> examples/validate_p95_values.rs:37:27
     |
  37 |         let is_positive = p95 >= 0;
     = help: because 0 is the minimum value for this type, this comparison is
       always true
     = note: #[deny(clippy::absurd_extreme_comparisons)] on by default

p95 is an unsigned type, so p95 >= 0 is a tautology and the guard does nothing.

This blocks bf-528j7: a clippy gate cannot be added to needle-ci until
--all-targets compiles. cargo clippy --tests is clean (exit 0, zero warnings)
as of 2fb89ed, so only the examples target is affected.

Fix: drop the tautological comparison, or make it a meaningful bound check if
the intent was to validate the value is non-zero / within range.

Acceptance: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 0.
close_reason: Fixed clippy error by removing tautological p95 >= 0 comparison. Since u128 is unsigned and always non-negative, the check was meaningless. Removed the comparison, the all_positive tracking, and updated comments to reflect that u128 is non-negative by definition. The fix commits as c0c01ba and has been pushed to origin.

title: Worker boot panics when telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true: tokio::spawn called outside runtime context

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
Reproduced 2026-08-08 on lab (100.81.129.38), 100% reproducible across both v0.2.16 and v0.2.19 binaries, so it's not a version regression — it's config-gated.

Root cause: src/cli/mod.rs (~line 826 in v0.2.19, ~741 in v0.2.16), inside the worker-boot tracing-subscriber init. When telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true, the OTLP branch calls tokio::spawn(async move { ... drop_rx.recv() ... }) to build the drop-event logging task — but this init function runs synchronously, before the worker's tokio runtime is entered. Panic: 'there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a Tokio 1.x runtime'. Every single worker-boot attempt crashed immediately after 'initializing tracing subscriber' in stderr, before ever reaching bead_store_discover.

needle rollback (0.2.19->0.2.16) hits the same class of bug on its own shutdown path (src/telemetry/otlp.rs:463), confirming this pattern isn't new.

Repro condition: config's telemetry.otlp_sink.enabled=true (lab's was pointed at http://needle-otel-lab-apexalgo-iad-ts.ardenone.com:4318). Workaround applied on lab: set otlp_sink.enabled=false in ~/.config/needle/config.yaml (original backed up to config.yaml.bak-otlp-panic-2026-08-08). Fix needed: move the tokio::spawn call to run after runtime entry (e.g. spawn from within the async worker-boot future, or use runtime.handle().spawn() with an explicitly-passed Handle, or build the drop-channel task via a plain OS thread instead of tokio::spawn).

title: classify_error_code has 153 duplicated error codes; 46 match arms unreachable
description:
Found 2026-08-02 while unblocking the v0.2.16 release.

src/types/mod.rs classify_error_code() enumerates 710 distinct Rust error
codes across category arms, but 153 of them appear more than once. Because
match arms are evaluated in order, the second and later occurrences are dead:
rustc reports 46 'unreachable pattern' errors under
cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings.

The practical effect is silent misclassification. E0748-E0757, for example,
are claimed by the Syntax arm and then listed again under 'Macro expansion
errors' — so they classify as Syntax, not Macro. Same for the E0750/E0758-E0761
overlap between ScopeVisibility and Macro, and E0781-E0783 between TraitImpl,
BorrowChecker and Macro.

This is not cosmetic: the whole point of the feature (bf-5pcn6/bf-59d0e/bf-5s7br)
is routing on error category, and 46 codes route to the wrong one.

The enumeration also covers codes rustc does not emit (E0800-E0999 are listed
wholesale as Syntax), which inflates the arms and makes the overlap hard to
see by eye.

Reproduce: cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings

Fix direction: derive the mapping from a single ordered table keyed by code so
duplicates are impossible by construction, or at minimum de-duplicate and add a
unit test asserting no code appears in more than one category. Trim codes rustc
never emits.

Note this merged unverified because needle-ci has been wedged since
2026-07-31 (declarative-config bf-2ls).

title: Fix needle-ci retryStrategy: it masks every failure as 'Max duration limit exceeded'
description:
Both failed runs on 2026-08-06 reported "Max duration limit exceeded" at the
workflow level. That is wrong and it cost real diagnosis time -- the actual
failure was exit code 101 from a single failing test.

Cause: retryStrategy.backoff.maxDuration is 10m, but one attempt takes 22-26 min.
maxDuration is the total retry budget measured from the first attempt, so retries
can never fire, and the retry machinery relabels an ordinary test failure with a
misleading message.

Secondary: retryPolicy is OnError, which would not retry a test failure anyway.
The transient-network case the template's comment justifies wants
OnTransientError.

Do, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
remove backoff.maxDuration (or raise it well above one attempt) and switch
retryPolicy to OnTransientError.

Acceptance: a failing test surfaces as a test failure with the failing test name,
not as a duration message.

  - The pod carries nodeSelector servers.ngpc.rxt.io/class=ch.vs1.large-iad,
    which excludes the three compute1-4 nodes (1500m / 2.6Gi) outright. Only the
    three compute1-8 nodes (3500m / 6.16Gi) are ever eligible.
  - Those three are not empty. They also host forgejo, eventbus-default-js,
    calico, armor and victorialogs. Free CPU at the time of writing was 900m,
    900m and 1100m; free memory 1820Mi, 988Mi and 1948Mi.
  - needle-ci requests 2000m CPU and 4Gi. It fits on none of them.
  - The dominant occupier was a single ACB build: acb-bots-build-5kv8k ran FIVE
    concurrent kaniko pods at 1000m/2048Mi each (5 CPU, 10Gi total), spread
    1/2/2 across exactly those three nodes, for 99+ minutes.

So one unrelated multi-container build can monopolise every node needle-ci is
allowed to run on, and needle-ci then burns its entire 2h deadline in Pending.
This is a scheduling failure, not a slow build, and it is invisible in the
"Failed" status -- the workflow reports a deadline breach with no logs.

The template comment says the 2000m/4Gi request was deliberately sized against
the biggest node. That reasoning accounted for node capacity but not for the
resident system pods or for concurrent workflows.

Options, in declarative-config k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/needle-workflowtemplate.yml:
  - lower the CPU request so the pod fits alongside normal residents (the limit
    can stay high -- requests gate scheduling, limits gate throttling)
  - drop the large-node selector once the request fits a compute1-4 node
  - cap ACB kaniko parallelism, or give CI workflows a PriorityClass so a
    release gate is not starved by an image build
  - shorten the effective runtime so the deadline is not spent queuing (see
    bf-4icmm, bf-4jdlu, bf-53ihi)

Acceptance: needle-ci reaches Running within a few minutes of submission even
while another multi-pod build is in flight.

title: 16.5b identity_pattern verification — reject the br shim masquerading as beads_rust
description:
~/.local/bin/br is a shell shim that logs the caller and execs ~/.local/bin/bf. The real beads_rust binary is ~/.cargo/bin/br v0.1.28. So `which br` returns something that speaks the bf dialect — this is exactly how ADR-013 section 5 went unnoticed for as long as it did.

A resolver that finds `br` on PATH and assumes beads_rust will bind the beads_rust adapter to bead-forge all over again, in a new place.

Deliverables:
- After resolving a candidate binary, VERIFY the backend identity rather than trusting the filename. `br --version` on the shim prints `bf <version>` (it execs bf), so a version-string check is sufficient and cheap — but confirm that empirically before relying on it.
- On mismatch (filename says br, identity says bf), fail loudly with an actionable message naming both paths. Do not silently fall back.
- Same check for a bf-named binary that is actually something else.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test with a fixture shim (a script execing a different fake binary) proves the mismatch is detected and reported, not silently accepted.
- The error message names the resolved path AND the identity actually found.

See ADR-013 section 5 and Evidence.

before 2026-08-06 12:35Z:

  node exit **101**

Exit 101 is the Rust convention for a panic / `cargo test` failure, so this
is a real red suite, not just the duration cap. The duration message means
the run also hit the workflow's max-duration before finishing.

Relates to the epic bf-21tze ("cut NEEDLE CI from a ~50min red run to a
<10min green run") — this bead records the concrete current failure so the
epic has a reproducible starting point rather than a general description.

At 12:35Z there were **four** needle-ci workflows queued simultaneously
(`needle-ci-8x2jj` 76m, `-f46kr` 69m, `-kz4qz` 62m, `-xt8tz` 62m), none of
them able to schedule a pod. Each push spawns another run while the previous
ones are still queued, so the queue grows faster than it drains. Consider a
concurrency limit / `synchronization` semaphore on the needle-ci template so
only one run is in flight per branch.

## Reproducing

Pod logs are gone (`podGC: OnPodCompletion`). Resubmit with a
`podGC: OnWorkflowCompletion` override, or stream logs while running.

description:

Currently `check_system_resources()` in `src/rate_limit/mod.rs` uses `tracing::warn!` log macros rather than structured telemetry events. This violates design principle 4 (Observable by default: every state transition emits structured telemetry) and the plan's event catalog is incomplete without these events.

- Add `FleetCpuSaturated { load_average: f64, threshold: f64, core_count: usize }` variant to `EventKind` in `src/telemetry/mod.rs`
- Add `FleetMemoryLow { free_mb: u64, threshold_mb: u64 }` variant to `EventKind`
- Update `check_system_resources()` in `src/rate_limit/mod.rs` to accept a `&Telemetry` sink and emit these events instead of (or in addition to) the tracing log
- Update call sites in `src/worker/mod.rs` to pass the telemetry sink
- Add the two event types to the telemetry documentation in `docs/plan/plan.md` (Health event catalog)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `fleet.cpu_saturated` event appears in JSONL log when load exceeds threshold
- [ ] `fleet.memory_low` event appears in JSONL log when free RAM drops below threshold
- [ ] Both events carry the numeric values (actual vs threshold) in their `data` field

title: Fix BfCliBeadStore::add_dependency — two positionals, bf 0.4.1 dep add takes one (bf store ONLY)
description:
BrCliBeadStore::add_dependency (src/bead_store/mod.rs:1579) and BfCliBeadStore::add_dependency (:2288) both emit `dep add <blocked> <blocker> --type blocks`. bf 0.4.1 signature is `bf dep add [OPTIONS] <BLOCKER>` — exactly ONE positional (the blocker), with the blocked bead passed as `--blocks <BLOCKS>`. `-t, --type` does exist and defaults to blocks.

So the second positional is an unexpected argument. Note prompt/mod.rs:325 already tells the agent the CORRECT form (`bf dep add <blocker-id> --blocks <blocked-id>`) — it is the store code that is stale, not the prompt.

Deliverables:
- Both impls emit `dep add <blocker> --blocks <blocked>`; drop the redundant explicit --type blocks (it is the default) or keep it as `-t blocks`, but verify against the installed bf first.
- Confirm argument ORDER semantics empirically before landing — get it backwards and dependency edges invert, which is worse than failing loudly.
- Same treatment for remove_dependency (:1667) — verify `bf dep remove` signature.
- Fixture-CLI argv assertion tests for add and remove.

Acceptance criteria:
- A real round-trip against a scratch .beads workspace proves the edge lands in the intended direction (blocker blocks blocked), not merely that the command exits 0.
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

See docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md, Addendum.

comments.author: cli
comments.text:
NARROWED 2026-08-11 — this bug is in the BF store only. BrCliBeadStore::add_dependency (:1579) is CORRECT and must not be touched.

Probed the real beads_rust binary (~/.cargo/bin/br v0.1.28, dicklesworthstone/beads_rust — NOT the ~/.local/bin/br shim, which execs bf):

  br  0.1.28: dep add <ISSUE> <DEPENDS_ON> -t blocks   -> TWO positionals
  bf  0.4.1 : dep add <BLOCKER> --blocks <BLOCKED> -t  -> ONE positional
  bead 0.1.0: dep add <BLOCKED> <BLOCKER> --kind blocks -> TWO positionals

br and bead agree on two positionals in (blocked, blocker) order. bf is the outlier. So BrCliBeadStore:1579 is right for its backend and BfCliBeadStore:2288 is wrong for its own.

REVISED SCOPE — only :2288 changes: dep add <blocker> --blocks <blocked>. Drop or keep -t blocks (it is the default on bf); verify against the installed binary, do not assume.

Also check remove_dependency in both stores against each backend before landing.

Acceptance criterion stands and is the important one: a real round-trip against a scratch .beads workspace must prove the edge lands in the intended direction (blocker blocks blocked), not merely that the command exits 0. Getting the order backwards inverts every dependency edge silently — worse than failing loudly. Verified reference for bf: `bf dep add bf-46m05 --blocks bf-2qm6r` prints "Added dependency: bf-2qm6r depends on bf-46m05 (blocks)".

See docs/adr/013-pluggable-bead-cli-backends.md section 2 (dialect matrix) and section 5.

title: 16.4c Author the bead-rs builtin descriptor
description:
New src/bead_store/bead_cli.rs implementing the existing BeadStore trait against bead-rs (`bead`). Surface enumerated from ~/bead-rs/src/cli.rs at commit fa30574.

Dialect specifics (each differs from bf in a way that fails loudly at runtime and silently in review):
- claim/release/clear_assignee: plain `update --status ... --assignee ...` / `update --status open --clear-assignee`. bead-rs UpdateOptions (cli.rs:444) KEPT the --assignee that bf 0.4.1 removed, so these are SIMPLER here than on bf — no batch emulation needed.
- claim_auto: `claim --assignee A --json`. Omit --model/--harness/--harness-version — bead-rs ClaimOptions (cli.rs:370) does not accept them. Selection falls back to bead-rs own --policy (default fifo-v1).
- create_bead: `--description` (not --body), repeated `--label`, no --json. bead-rs create prints the bare issue ID on stdout.
- add_dependency: `--kind blocks` (not --type). Confirm positional order against the installed binary before landing.
- full_rebuild: bead-rs `sync --import-only` REQUIRES --input plus exactly one of --restore-into-empty / --merge (SyncCommand, cli.rs:667). The current bare call would fail.
- list/show/update --status/reopen/close --reason/label add|remove/doctor [--repair]/sync --flush-only all match and need no special handling.
- split_bead: deliberately NOT overridden. bead-rs has no `batch` subcommand, so it inherits the non-atomic trait default (:646-668) and its documented orphaned-child crash window. Log at split time that the atomic path is unavailable on this backend.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every trait method implemented; no todo!()/unimplemented!().
- Known limitations (no atomic split, no velocity-scoring metadata) are logged at runtime, not silently swallowed.
- fmt + clippy + full suite green on iad-ci.

comments.text:

Unlike br and bf, bead-rs publishes NO GitHub releases — it is Forgejo-only (git.ardenone.com/jedarden/bead-rs). There is no release artifact to pin to, so this descriptor must name a COMMIT.

title: is_pid_alive treats zombie workers as alive, fooling supervisor capacity accounting (GH #12, compounding)
description:
Compounding half of GH #12 (https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/12), same report as bf-12bim (reap sweep). Full rationale: ADR-010 (docs/adr/010-supervisor-zombie-reaping.md), plan.md Phase 14.2.

Confirmed against source: registry::is_pid_alive (src/registry/mod.rs:28-52) checks liveness via kill(pid, 0) == 0 (with errno ESRCH/EPERM disambiguation). kill(pid, 0) succeeds for a zombie (state Z) exactly as it does for a genuinely running process — a zombie still holds a PID table entry, it just hasn't been reaped yet (see bf-12bim). This is not a hypothetical concern: Supervisor::tick() (src/supervisor/mod.rs:308-336) filters registered workers with is_pid_alive(w.pid) (line 316) to compute alive_count, then gates new spawns on alive_count >= self.config.max_workers (line 335). So every unreaped worker zombie is counted as alive by the supervisor's own tick, artificially inflating alive_count and potentially blocking new worker spawns at exactly the moment real capacity exists. The reporter's issue explicitly connects this to a 'false max_workers capacity and silent hung supervise logs' observation during their cutover soak (compounded on their host by an unrelated large zombie population from PID 1 not reaping its own children).

strand::mend's liveness check (src/strand/mend.rs:707) also calls registry::is_pid_alive and inherits this same bug.

Suggested fix (decision in ADR-010): on Linux, additionally check /proc/<pid>/stat's process-state field (the character after the second ')' in the comm field, robust to command names containing parentheses) and treat state Z as NOT alive, even though kill(pid, 0) still succeeds for it. Fall back to today's kill(pid, 0)-only behavior on non-Linux platforms (no /proc on macOS) and whenever /proc/<pid>/stat is unreadable for any reason (permissions, race with process exit) — never MORE strict than today's check, only additionally strict for the one case (Z) that today's check gets provably wrong.

Explicitly out of scope (per ADR-010): src/cli/mod.rs has its own separate, simpler duplicate is_pid_alive (kill(pid,0)==0, no errno handling) used for needle status/needle cleanup display/filtering, not supervisor capacity gating. It has the same zombie blind spot in principle but fixing it is not necessary to resolve GH #12's reported impact — leave it as a smaller, separate follow-up if status/cleanup output for zombies becomes its own complaint.

Acceptance criteria:
- registry::is_pid_alive returns false for a deliberately-created, deliberately-unreaped zombie PID on Linux.
- Behavior unchanged for non-Linux platforms and for genuinely-alive/genuinely-dead PIDs on all platforms (existing liveness tests still pass).
- Regression test reproducing the reporter's capacity-hang scenario: a zombie worker in the registry no longer counts toward alive_count in Supervisor::tick().
- cargo test --lib passes; no clippy warnings; needle-ci green on push.
close_reason: Fixed by 81b0995 (bf-z3yp0): registry::is_pid_alive now checks /proc/<pid>/stat state on Linux and treats Z (zombie) as not-alive, so Supervisor::tick()'s alive_count/max_workers capacity gate can no longer be fooled by unreaped zombies. GH #12.
